name: Jacint Verdaguer
credit: Portrait of Jacint Verdaguer by Ramon Casas (MNAC) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Jacint Verdaguer i Santaló was born in 1845 at Folgueroles, in the Catalan county of Osona, to a farming family. He trained for the priesthood at Vic, was ordained in 1870, and later served as chaplain to a Barcelona shipping line while he wrote.

His epic L'Atlàntida (1877) and the Pyrenean legend Canigó (1886) made him the leading poet of the Catalan Renaixença and gave the revived literary language a new classical register. He died at Vallvidrera, near Barcelona, in 1902, mourned as a national poet.
